label: input token g during copy phase (and weakly at t=0)
explanation: Token detector for input g. Fires on every copy-phase step whose fed-back input is g, at about 0.6-0.96 of max. Activations are highest at recall positions 1-2 (right after <DEL>) and on the first of two adjacent gs. When g is the first original token (t=0) it fires weakly at a constant ~0.25 of max. It fires only sometimes, and weakly, on g at t=1, and almost never on g later in the original phase. It never fires at the delimiter step. Tiny off-target activations (~0.1 of max) on b/x inputs hold <1% of mass. Copy phase g alone: precision 1.0, recall 0.78, mass recall 0.93; adding t=0 brings F1 to 0.96.

issues: Precision claim holds: on test, the predicate (g input at t=0 or in the copy phase) has 0 false positives, so the feature really does fire on every copy-phase g and every g at t=0.

The remaining misses are minor and match the explanation. g at t=1: the feature fires on 27% of these steps, only weakly (always in the lowest activation quartile), for 0.8% of mass. g at t>=2 in the original phase: 0.4% firing rate, 0.06% of mass. b/x inputs: 0.5% of mass. Together the misses hold 1.5% of test mass, which is scattered noise.

Magnitude claims are only weakly supported. Copy-phase g at recall_idx<=2 averages only about 5% more mass per step than at recall_idx>=3, so 'highest at recall 1-2' is true but the effect is small. The t=0 activation is constant at 0.25 of max in all the examples shown.
Adding t==1 to the predicate raises mass recall to 0.994 but drops precision to 0.90 and F1 to 0.933, so the original predicate is the better choice. No systematic class of counterexamples remains.
